title: Definite Integration
description: Class 12 IMO — Definite Integration: the definite integral and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, properties of definite integrals, and evaluation as a limit of a sum.

topics.title: Definite Integral and the FTC
topics.concept:
The definite integral $\displaystyle\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$ is a number — the net signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis from $a$ to $b$.

Fundamental Theorem of Calculus

If $F$ is an antiderivative of $f$, then

$$\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=F(b)-F(a).$$

So you integrate, then substitute the limits and subtract. The constant $C$ cancels, which is why definite integrals have no $+C$.

Useful properties

  • $\displaystyle\int_a^b f\,dx=-\int_b^a f\,dx$, and $\displaystyle\int_a^a f\,dx=0$.
  • $\displaystyle\int_a^b f\,dx=\int_a^c f\,dx+\int_c^b f\,dx$.
  • $\displaystyle\int_0^a f(x)\,dx=\int_0^a f(a-x)\,dx$ (the "king" property).
  • $\displaystyle\int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx=2\int_0^a f\,dx$ if $f$ is even, and $0$ if $f$ is odd.

examples.solution: $x^3$ is an odd function and the limits are symmetric, so by the odd-function property the integral is $0$.

recap: $\int_a^b f\,dx=F(b)-F(a)$ (Fundamental Theorem); no $+C$ for definite integrals.
Swapping limits flips the sign; equal limits give $0$.

quiz.explanation: |x| is even, so ∫₋₂² |x| dx = 2 ∫₀² x dx = 2 · [x²/2]₀² = 2 · 2 = 4.

quiz.q: If f(x) is continuous and ∫₀ˣ f(t) dt = x² + 2x, then f(2) equals:
quiz.explanation: By FTC, differentiating both sides: f(x) = 2x + 2. So f(2) = 4 + 2 = 6.

topics.title: Properties of Definite Integrals
topics.concept:
Key properties: ∫[a,b] f = −∫[b,a] f; ∫[a,b] f = ∫[a,c] f + ∫[c,b] f; and ∫[0,a] f(x)dx = ∫[0,a] f(a−x)dx.

Symmetry: ∫[−a,a] f = 0 if f is odd, and 2∫[0,a] f if f is even.
recap: Odd function over [−a, a] integrates to 0.

quiz.q: The value of ∫₀² x² [x] dx, where [x] is greatest integer function, is:
quiz.explanation: ∫₀² x² [x] dx = ∫₀¹ x²·0 dx + ∫₁² x²·1 dx = 0 + [x³/3]₁² = 8/3 − 1/3 = 7/3. We check: x in [0,1): [x]=0. x in [1,2): [x]=1. At x=2, [2]=2 but point measure zero. So ∫ = 0 + ∫₁² x² dx = [x³/3]₁² = 8/3 − 1/3 = 7/3. Option 3 is 7/3. So correct index 3.

quiz.q: The area bounded by y = sin 2x, x = 0, x = π/2 and the x-axis is:
quiz.explanation: Area = ∫₀^(π/2) |sin 2x| dx. sin 2x ≥ 0 in [0, π/2], so area = ∫₀^(π/2) sin 2x dx = [−1/2 cos 2x]₀^(π/2) = −1/2(−1 − 1) = 1.

topics.title: Integral as a Limit of a Sum
topics.concept:
The definite integral is the limit of a Riemann sum: ∫[a,b] f(x)dx = lim (b−a)/n · Σ f(a + r(b−a)/n) as n → ∞.

This first-principles view links integration to area accumulation.

examples.problem: What does the Riemann sum approximate?
examples.solution: The area under the curve between a and b.

examples.problem: As n → ∞, the sum tends to?

recap: ∫ = limit of Riemann sums as n → ∞.

quiz.q: The area enclosed by y = √x, x = 1, x = 4 and the x-axis is:
A steel plant in Bhilai has a production rate given by P'(t) = 50 + 4t tonnes/hour. What is the total steel produced in the first 5 hours?
quiz.explanation: Total production = ∫[0 to 5] (50 + 4t) dt = [50t + 2t²] from 0 to 5 = 250 + 2(25) = 250 + 50 = 300 tonnes.

questions.q: What is the area of the circle x² + y² = a² using definite integration in the first quadrant?
questions.explanation: The area in the first quadrant is ∫[0 to a] √(a² - x²) dx. Using the standard formula, it evaluates to (πa²)/4.
This converts to ∫[0 to 1] x² dx. Evaluating this gives [x³/3] from 0 to 1 = 1/3.

questions.q: If ∫₀¹ (x² + kx + 1) dx = 1, then k equals:
Determine the area of the region bounded by the curve y = 2x - x² and the x-axis.
questions.explanation: The curve intersects the x-axis at x = 0 and x = 2. Area = ∫[0 to 2] (2x - x²) dx = [x² - x³/3] from 0 to 2 = (4 - 8/3) - 0 = 4/3.

questions.q: A decorative garden patch in Kerala is shaped as the area bounded by y = sin x, x = 0, x = π, and the x-axis. What is the area of this patch in square units?
questions.explanation: Area = ∫[0 to π] sin x dx = [-cos x] from 0 to π = -(-1) - (-1) = 1 + 1 = 2 square units.

questions.q: A sweet shop sells boxes of laddoos. The demand function is p(x) = 100 - x², where x is the quantity. If the equilibrium quantity is 6 boxes, what is the Consumer Surplus? (Assume equilibrium price is p(6))
questions.explanation: Equilibrium price = 100 - 36 = 64. Consumer Surplus = ∫[0 to 6] (100 - x² - 64) dx = ∫[0 to 6] (36 - x²) dx = [36x - x³/3] from 0 to 6 = 216 - 72 = 144.

questions.q: Evaluate the integral involving the greatest integer function: ∫[0 to 1.5] [x] dx.
questions.explanation: Split the integral where the integer value changes: ∫[0 to 1] 0 dx + ∫[1 to 1.5] 1 dx = 0 + [x] from 1 to 1.5 = 1.5 - 1 = 0.5.
|cos x| is positive. ∫₀^π |cos x| dx = ∫₀^(π/2) cos x dx + ∫_(π/2)^π (−cos x) dx = [sin x]₀^(π/2) + [−sin x]_(π/2)^π = (1−0) + (0−(−1)) = 2.

questions.q: Using the property of definite integrals, evaluate ∫[0 to π/2] (sin x)/(sin x + cos x) dx.
questions.explanation: Let I = ∫[0 to π/2] (sin x)/(sin x + cos x) dx. Using property ∫[0 to a] f(x) dx = ∫[0 to a] f(a-x) dx, I = ∫[0 to π/2] (cos x)/(cos x + sin x) dx. Adding both gives 2I = ∫[0 to π/2] 1 dx = π/2. So, I = π/4.

questions.q: If ∫₀¹ xˣ dx = ∫₀¹ (1 − x)ˣ dx, then the value of α is:
questions.explanation: Let I = ∫₀¹ xˣ dx. Put x = 1 − t, dx = −dt. Limits: 0→1, 1→0. I = ∫₁⁰ (1−t)ˣ (−dt) = ∫₀¹ (1−t)ˣ dt. So equality holds for any α. The variable of integration is dummy; the integral of xˣ from 0 to 1 equals integral of (1−x)ˣ from 0 to 1 by substitution, regardless of α.

questions.q: If ∫[0 to 1] f(x) dx = 5 and ∫[0 to 1] g(x) dx = 2, find ∫[0 to 1] [3f(x) - 2g(x)] dx.
Water flows into an overhead tank in Mumbai at a rate of R(t) = 10e^(0.2t) liters/minute. How much water is added to the tank in the first 5 minutes?
questions.explanation: Volume = ∫[0 to 5] 10e^(0.2t) dt = [10/0.2 e^(0.2t)] from 0 to 5 = 50[e¹ - e⁰] = 50(e - 1) liters.
